SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
NELDA HOWTON'S BRIEF ON REMAND
PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Intervenor Nelda Howton, appearing pro se, submits this Brief on Remand concerning Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13. The Commission has asked SOAH to address whether the proposed facilities are necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards and what congestion-cost savings consumers may receive from these facilities. The evidentiary record is not being reopened. Mrs. Howton therefore asks that these questions be answered only from evidence already contained in the record.
I. ISSUE 11 - THE RECORD DOES NOT SHOW THAT THIS PARTICULAR 765-KV PROJECT IS REQUIRED
There is an important difference between showing that Texas may need additional transmission and proving that this particular Bell County East-Big Hill 765-kV project is necessary to meet a state or federal reliability standard. The existing record does not make that second showing.
ERCOT's Permian Basin Reliability Plan considered 345-kV, 500-kV, and 765-kV alternatives. ERCOT reported that all three alternatives satisfied the applicable ERCOT and NERC reliability criteria in the studied case. The 765-kV alternative provided greater transfer capability, but greater capacity is not the same as proving that 765 kV is required to meet a reliability standard. (CCN Application, Item Nos. 65 and 67, Attachment 1 and Attachment 5; PBRP Table E.1 / Table 7.6.)
Moreover, the Permian Basin Reliability Plan is a planning study, not independent validation of actual, current congestion or of the necessity of this particular project. The Plan relied on 2023-era data, forecasts, and assumptions. The existing evidentiary record does not identify an independent professional engineer who separately verified those underlying congestion assumptions, forecasts, or inputs before they were used to support the claimed need for this 765-kV project. A planning model based on older assumptions may support further study, but it does not, standing alone, establish present congestion or prove that this specific facility is necessary to satisfy a reliability standard.
The age of the underlying information is significant because a planning forecast is only as reliable as the data and assumptions on which it rests. The existing record does not show that the 2023-era assumptions were revalidated to determine whether the same load growth, generation, retirement, transmission, or congestion conditions remained accurate when this CCN application was considered. Nor does the record identify an independent professional engineer who separately confirmed that the projected congestion actually existed or that the same conditions continued to support the claimed need for these particular facilities. ERCOT's selection of a transmission concept for planning purposes does not relieve the Applicants of their separate burden in this CCN proceeding to prove, with competent evidence in this record, that these particular 765-kV facilities are necessary.
The question before SOAH is not simply whether more transmission could be useful. The question is whether these proposed 765-kV facilities are necessary. The record does not establish that 345-kV or 500-kV alternatives failed the applicable reliability standards.
The record may support a broader need for additional transmission capacity under certain forecast assumptions, but it does not establish that this specific 765-kV facility was the only solution capable of meeting the applicable reliability requirements.
Answer to Issue 11
Mrs. Howton respectfully submits that the existing evidentiary record does not establish that the proposed Bell County East-Big Hill 765-kV transmission facilities are necessary to meet a state or federal reliability standard.
II. ISSUE 13 - THE RECORD DOES NOT PROVIDE A PROJECT-SPECIFIC ESTIMATE OF CONSUMER CONGESTION SAVINGS
Issue 13 asks what congestion-cost savings consumers may receive from these proposed facilities. The record does not provide a project-specific dollar amount answering that question.
The PFD discusses Issue 13 and the economic evidence in the record. ERCOT economic studies compare broader transmission plans, including statewide 345-kV and 765-kV alternatives. Those studies may show possible benefits from a larger transmission plan, but they do not identify how much congestion savings would be produced specifically by the Bell County East-Big Hill project. (PFD, Item No. 6441, pp. 133-150; Gurley Direct, Item No. 5213, Ex. JG-4.)
The same evidentiary problem applies to congestion. Reliance on 2023-era planning data and modeled forecasts is not the same as validating actual present congestion. The record does not identify an independent engineering verification of the congestion assumptions or a project-specific validation showing that the modeled congestion remains accurate and is attributable to the Bell County East-Big Hill facilities.
If the congestion assumptions themselves depend on older forecast conditions that were not independently validated in this record, then the claimed economic benefits derived from those assumptions necessarily depend on the same unverified foundation. A forecast of future congestion is not the same as proof of actual present congestion, and a system-wide planning estimate is not a substitute for evidence showing the amount of congestion caused or relieved by this particular project.
Applicants' discovery response also does not provide a calculation separating the economic benefit of this individual project from the benefits claimed for the larger transmission system. (Applicants' Response to RFI Set 2, Item No. 5460.)
A system-wide economic benefit cannot simply be assigned to one project without evidence showing what portion of that benefit is actually caused by that project. The record does not provide a calculation showing the amount of present or future congestion attributable to this project, how much would actually be reduced by Bell County East-Big Hill, and the resulting dollar savings to consumers attributable specifically to this facility.
Answer to Issue 13
Mrs. Howton respectfully submits that the existing record does not contain a quantified project-specific estimate of congestion-cost savings to consumers attributable to the proposed Bell County East-Big Hill facilities.
III. THE CLOSED RECORD SHOULD CONTROL THE DECISION
The Commission remanded Issues 11 and 13 for additional consideration, but the evidentiary record is not being reopened. The decision therefore should be based on what was actually proven in the existing record, not on new evidence offered after the hearing.
That record does not establish that this particular 765-kV project is required to meet a reliability standard, and it does not provide a project-specific estimate of congestion-cost savings to consumers.
The remand cannot be used to supply proof that was absent when the evidentiary record closed. If the existing record does not contain current validation of the congestion assumptions, independent verification of the underlying data, or project-specific evidence establishing necessity and consumer savings, those deficiencies cannot now be cured by argument or by relying on the planning study as though it were independent proof of those facts.
Texas Government Code § 2001.058(e) limits an agency's authority to change an ALJ's finding of fact or conclusion of law and requires the statutory basis and specific reason for such a change to be stated in writing. The existing findings should not be displaced unless the existing record provides a legal and evidentiary basis for doing so.
IV. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
Nelda Howton respectfully asks the Administrative Law Judges to find that: (1) the existing evidentiary record does not establish that the proposed Bell County East-Big Hill 765-kV transmission facilities are necessary to meet a state or federal reliability standard under Preliminary Order Issue 11; (2) the record contains no quantified project-specific estimate of congestion-cost savings to consumers attributable to these proposed facilities under Preliminary Order Issue 13; and (3) the record contains no independently validated, current, project-specific evidence demonstrating congestion that requires this particular facility.
The burden was on the Applicants to establish these matters in the evidentiary record. Because that record is now closed, missing project-specific proof should not be supplied after the hearing. Mrs. Howton therefore respectfully requests that the supplemental or amended Proposal for Decision continue to recommend denial of the CCN application, together with all other relief to which she may be entitled.
Respectfully submitted,
